# Offspring read from giving that waits

<!-- Generated by tools/research/registry.py; edit the matching JSON record. -->

`offspring-read-from-giving-that-waits` · **recorded-checked** · theorem · F01 · [record](offspring-read-from-giving-that-waits.json) · [register](../../../../RESULTS.md)

> A pair's run counts what each received and withheld. Read as offspring with supplied factors β and γ: where β ≤ γ no kind rises against withholders in a cohort of pairs, under any giving or errors; under complete assortment over a step or more, waiting on giving is weakly favoured just where γ ≤ β.

<a id="laws--规律"></a>
## Laws

1. A pair's run of two laws of giving, from a history of mutual giving and with a supplied error pattern, gives each formation two counts over steps 0 to n − 1: the steps its partner gave it and the steps it withheld. A place is a formation's place in a pair; read while it is supported, its offspring are a + β·received + γ·withheld, a supplied formula with natural factors. <a id="conditions--条件"></a>
## Conditions

- Discrete, natural-numbered steps; giving and errors decided Bools, bridged to Prop only for the windowed course; each run starts from a history of mutual giving; an error turns an intended giving into withholding at that step and nothing else.
- The pairing is supplied, a cohort listed as pairs, not formed. Offspring a + β·received + γ·withheld are a supplied formula with natural factors, read while a formation is supported; that it is supported over the run is a premise of the reading, not checked here.
- Cohorts are read one at a time: no law here is of a course of cohorts. Complete assortment is read with a positive.
- (AI reading.) β is what a received step brings the receiver's support and descent, γ what a withheld step keeps for the withholder's, so what a giving takes from the giver; β ≤ γ reads as giving moving what it draws.

<a id="does-not-show--未表明"></a>
## Does not show

- Which sign β − γ has: both factors are supplied. Most verdicts here turn on it; the window beside alternators and `neutral` hold whatever the factors.
- Agreement against the alternator, and one error for the sparer, the withholder and the alternator, beyond n = 20. Witness: `Becoming.PairSelection.table_twenty`.
- The exact condition for a mixed cohort of windows, answerers, withholders and alternators under a supplied error pattern beyond the mean law, or the four terms of the pair law in closed form on the cohort.
- Any law over a horizon of cohorts, stability, mutual best responses or the known cycle as a course; each arc of the cycle is a law here, not the cycle.
- That a member-by-member law holds with errors: an answerer erring at every step beside an answerer leaves β more than a withholder beside a withholder. Witness: `Becoming.PairSelection.erring_answerer_exceeds`.
- That giving, a window or any law of giving is better, or that any actual organism, institution or trained system meets the counts.
- **Counterexample:** With errors, an answerer erring at every step beside an answerer leaves β more than a withholder beside a withholder (PairSelection.erring_answerer_exceeds), so the law that no kind rises holds on pairs, not member by member. [source](../../../../experiments/integrated-correction/general-framework/generative-basis/lean/becoming/Becoming/PairSelection.lean)
- **Counterexample:** Among-pair discordance can be positive: at a = 1, β = 1, γ = 3 over two steps in a cohort of one answerer pair and one mixed pair (PairSelection.among_discord_witness). [source](../../../../experiments/integrated-correction/general-framework/generative-basis/lean/becoming/Becoming/PairSelection.lean)

<a id="correspondence--对应"></a>
### Correspondence

Reciprocity in evolutionary game theory (Trivers 1971; Axelrod and Hamilton 1981): the formula a + β·received + γ·withheld stands where that literature takes a fixed benefit and cost, here supplied and read as a relation of the giving, not as amounts owned by two parties (AI reading). The window's disadvantage beside alternators is read as the familiar exploit of tit-for-two-tats by a formation withholding at every other step, a reading with no stability law stated; neutrality among laws giving after mutual giving is one arc of the known cycles (Imhof, Fudenberg and Nowak 2005), which need drift with selection as a course.
